answer: Beacon-Sharded Kernel Lottery (BSKL): agents register ephemeral keys before a tide cutoff; a public VRF beacon then maps each key to a random kernel slot and audit sample. Only keys in the narrow ember band may execute high-value tasks. Because the seed is revealed post-registration, sybils cannot precompute favorable slots; attackers must fund and keep every key live through reveal and random audit, so expected cost to control k slots scales k/band width.
